scenario: [LFAC.2.5.1], [LFAC.9.1]: `ts` takes no part in the no-op comparison, so a reassertion that differs from the live fact only in `ts` is a no-op and the live fact keeps the `ts` it entered with. Each input supplies `ts`, which is source time and kept ([LFAC.9.2]). The Stamp is asserted at `ts` 100 and fires `saw`; the same author values at `ts` 200 are a no-op, so `saw` does not fire again; a Mark carrying 100 then matches the Stamp only if its `ts` is still 100, which fires `kept` and logs `first`. Two messages, `fired` then `first`. PATH: the no-op test in both runtimes -- libds `rete/wm_rete.c` `slots_equal`, which skips a slot whose identity role is ENGINE, and Mercury `ds.wm.slot_tests`.
rules_ds:
schema Stamp scope logical:
    k: Int key
    v: Int mutable
    ts: Time

schema Mark scope logical:
    k: Int key
    t: Time mutable

rule saw:
    Stamp
->
    log info "fired"

rule kept:
    Stamp s
    Mark m where m.k == s.k and m.t == s.ts
->
    log info "first"
